title: Butyrate
summary: A short-chain fatty acid produced when gut bacteria (e.g. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Roseburia) ferment dietary fiber; the primary energy source for colon cells. Strengthens the gut barrier, crosses the blood-brain barrier, and supports weight, blood sugar and inflammation control.

details.what_it_is: A short-chain fatty acid produced when gut bacteria (e.g. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Roseburia) ferment dietary fiber; it is the primary energy source for colon cells.
details.gut_barrier: Keeps tight junctions strong and maintains the mucus layer, preventing undigested food, bacteria, and toxins from leaking into the bloodstream and triggering systemic inflammation.
systemic_benefits: Crosses the blood-brain barrier (linked to lower Alzheimer's risk via Eubacterium / Eisenbergiella)
Supports weight management and blood sugar control via hunger hormones
Promotes apoptosis in damaged colon cells (lower colorectal cancer risk)

diet: A diverse range of fiber sources (fruits, vegetables, whole grains, beans)
Fermented foods (kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi, grass-fed yogurt)
cautions: Increase fiber gradually if gut health is compromised, to avoid endotoxin buildup
Ensure mitochondrial function is optimal first
